title: W-3b: refuse or flag request-rewriting override headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-Original-URL, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-Host); needs opum-doc design
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-3 (second half), sec-b F2. The Host and framing names of W-3 are delivered by WCLI-84 (opum-ai/ward-cli#208, DEC-248); no duplicate is filed. DEC-248 does not rule on the override headers, which several frameworks honour, so an approved method GET can execute as DELETE. Design question for opum-doc: refuse, or flag prominently in the approval prompt, which names, and the snapshot-version consequence. Not buildable until a design is recorded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: opum-doc records a design for override headers: refuse or flag, the exact name set, and the version policy
The recorded design is implemented with tests in both directions, and profileSnapshotVersion follows ADR 0018

implementationNotes: DESIGN RULING, opum-doc, 2026-10-30T15:57:41Z, recorded on ODOC-552, relayed by team-lead. Verbatim: "REFUSE them; do not flag. Use the same reserved-name mechanism as W-3/WCLI-84: case-insensitive, at profile validation. The refused set: X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-HTTP-Method, X-Method-Override, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-For and Forwarded. Reason: each one lets the request differ from what the approval prompt showed (method, path or authority), and a prompt flag is the layout surface W-5 already shows can be spoofed. An existing profile that declares one is refused on load with an error naming the header, under the snapshot-version policy, never silently stripped. If a real API needs one later, that is a new design ask, not an exception in code." The first acceptance criterion (opum-doc records a design) is met by this ruling; the build is briefed separately after its floor check.

Opus review of ward-cli#208 (verbatim): "landing WCLI-98 separately means profileSnapshotVersion 4 and a second fleet re-approval; its refused set must also apply to auth.name, not only to ordinary headers, since both now share isRefusedHeaderName (profile.ts:232-235)."

opum-doc ruling, 2026-10-30T16:29:41Z (to be recorded on ODOC-552), verbatim: "FOLD WCLI-98 into WCLI-84's snapshot version. One profile re-approval for the operator, not two.
- No Ward release (no tag, no main promotion) is cut until WCLI-98 has landed on dev alongside #208. Both changes ride one profileSnapshotVersion. If #208 has already bumped it to 3, WCLI-98 stays at 3 rather than going to 4, which is safe because nothing at 3 has been released or approved anywhere.
- Yes, the refused set covers auth.name through the shared isRefusedHeaderName: a secret header may not be named any of the nine override headers, Host, or the framing and hop-by-hop names. Prove it both ways in WCLI-98's tests.
- Plan the operator's single sitting to cover everything that forces a re-approval: these snapshot changes and the W-1 rebuild, whose new cdhash needs the keychain approved again (WCLI-96). Batch them into one release and one sitting, not three." This SUPERSEDES the preceding note's "profileSnapshotVersion 4 and a second fleet re-approval" observation (reviewer, ward-cli#208); both are kept so the record shows each. The refused-set-covers-auth.name half of that earlier note stands. Not built; WCLI-98 gets its own floor-checked brief after #208 lands.

Built on feat/wcli-98-refuse-override-headers per the 15:57:41Z and 16:29:41Z rulings: the nine names added to refusedHeaderNames (profile.ts), shared by ordinary headers and auth.name via isRefusedHeaderName; profileSnapshotVersion stays 3. Tests in test/header-auth.test.ts: each name as written/lower/upper in both positions, near names accepted, version asserted 3, stored v3 snapshot declaring one refused as vault_state_malformed (with positive control). Mutation control: removing x-rewrite-url turned exactly its 6 cases red. ADR 0024 amended. bun run check green (923 pass). Open design gap: the ruling says the load error names the header, but no Ward error carries a header name (WardError holds a code and an argument position only), so refusal reports profile_invalid or vault_state_malformed with no name; reported to team-lead.
